questions.q: True or False? 'According to the chapter, in every market goods and services can be exchanged only for money.' Give the verdict and a reason.

questions.q: What are economic activities? Give one example from the chapter.
questions.a: Economic activities are those that involve money, or are performed in exchange for money or money's worth, for the parties involved. Example: a farmer selling produce in the market (or a lawyer arguing a case and earning a fee, a truck driver transporting goods, a business person selling school bags, workers in a car manufacturing factory).
s: Definition: activities that involve money or are performed in exchange for money or money's worth
One correct example from the chapter, such as a lawyer earning a fee or a farmer selling produce

questions.q:
Each of these people is doing an economic activity. For each, write the form of payment that makes it economic: a sale in the market, a fee, or a salary.
(a) A tea-stall owner at Howrah station selling cups of tea to travellers.
(b) A chartered accountant in Pune charging a shopkeeper for advice on filing taxes.
(c) A welder employed in a bus-body factory in Bengaluru, paid a fixed amount every month by the factory.
questions.a: (a) A sale in the market: the tea is sold to travellers for money. (b) A fee: a payment for professional advice. (c) A salary: a fixed regular payment, paid monthly by an employer to an employee.
s: (a) A sale: tea sold for money
(b) A fee: payment for professional advice
(c) A salary: fixed monthly payment from the employer

questions.q: Kiran says: 'Geeta Aunty flies for the Indian Air Force to serve the country, so her work is service like seva and cannot be an economic activity.' Check Kiran's claim using the chapter.
questions.a: Kiran is wrong. The chapter says Geeta Aunty receives a salary, so she performs an economic activity too, while she serves the country; serving the country and doing economic activity go together. Seva is different because it is selfless service done without expecting anything in return, whereas Geeta Aunty is paid a salary for her work.
s: Verdict: the claim is wrong
Geeta Aunty receives a salary, so her work is an economic activity even though she serves the country
Seva is done without expecting anything in return, so her salaried work is not seva

questions.q:
Dr. Farida is a veterinary doctor in Lucknow. In one week she does four things:
(i) Monday to Friday she works at a government animal hospital, which pays her a fixed amount at the end of every month.
(ii) On Saturday evening she treats pets at her own clinic, and each owner pays her for the check-up.
(iii) On Sunday morning she checks stray dogs in her colony free of charge, out of care for them.
(iv) On Sunday afternoon she cooks lunch for her parents.
(a) Classify each of the four activities as economic or non-economic.
(b) Name the form of payment in (i) and in (ii), and state how the two differ.
(c) Her neighbour says, 'Her Sunday work with the stray dogs is worth less to the colony than her clinic work, because it earns nothing.' Do you agree? Give a reason from the chapter.
questions.a: (a) (i) and (ii) are economic, because they are done in exchange for money; (iii) and (iv) are non-economic, because they earn no income and are done out of care and love. (b) (i) is a salary, a fixed regular payment paid monthly by an employer to an employee; (ii) is a fee, a payment made to a person in exchange for professional services, paid by each owner for each check-up. (c) Disagree. The chapter says non-economic activities may not involve money, but the value they generate is important in our lives; her free care of the stray dogs is done out of care and helps the colony even though it earns nothing.
s: (a) (i) and (ii) economic: done in exchange for money
(a) (iii) and (iv) non-economic: no income, done out of care and love
(b) (i) is a salary: fixed regular monthly payment from an employer
(b) (ii) is a fee: payment for professional services, paid by each owner
(c) Disagrees: non-economic activities may not involve money but the value they generate is important

questions.q: Which ONE of these is a non-economic activity, as the chapter uses the term?
questions.a: An uncle teaching his nephew to ride a bicycle in the park
o: An uncle teaching his nephew to ride a bicycle in the park
A cycle mechanic in Agra mending a punctured tyre for Rs 50
A coach at a sports academy who is paid every month

questions.a: They earn no income or wealth but are done out of love, care and respect
o: They earn no income or wealth but are done out of love, care and respect
They are done only by people who have no paid job or business of their own
They are paid for with goods, such as fruit or grain, instead of with cash
They are small tasks that need very little time, skill or effort from anyone

questions.q: Mr. Das teaches Mathematics to his own daughter every evening. On Sunday mornings he teaches the same topic to four children from his street, and each of them pays him Rs 200. Which statement describes his two activities correctly?
questions.a: The evening teaching is non-economic; the Sunday teaching is economic
o: The evening teaching is non-economic; the Sunday teaching is economic
Both are economic, because teaching is a job that teachers are paid for
Both are non-economic, because he teaches the same topic both times
The evening teaching is economic; the Sunday teaching is non-economic

questions.q:

I. He is a software engineer in a company that makes computer applications.
II. On weekends he teaches computer skills at the nearby college's youth development programme and is paid a weekly fee for it.

Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only
o: I and III only
I and II only
II and III only
I, II and III

questions.q: True or False? 'In the chapter, the same kind of work, teaching, is an economic activity for one person and a non-economic activity for another.' Give the verdict and a reason.
questions.a: True. Rohan teaches computer skills on weekends as a volunteer, which the chapter calls a non-economic activity, while Kavya's aunt conducts online classes in the evening and charges a weekly fee for them, which is an economic activity. What decides it is whether money is involved.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: Rohan's unpaid weekend teaching is non-economic, while Kavya's aunt's fee-charging online classes are economic

questions.q: What are non-economic activities? Name two examples that the chapter gives.
questions.a: Non-economic activities are those that do not generate income or wealth but are done out of feelings like gratitude, love, care and respect. Examples: parents cooking food for the family, parents helping their children with schoolwork, youth taking care of the grandparents, family members helping in the renovation of the house (any two).
s: Definition: do not generate income or wealth; done out of gratitude, love, care and respect
Any two of the chapter's examples, such as parents cooking for the family and youth caring for grandparents

questions.q:
Kabir's grandfather retired from the Border Security Force. He now gives free Geography classes to the neighbourhood kids.
(a) Is his Geography teaching an economic or a non-economic activity?
(b) Give the reason for your answer.

questions.a: (a) Non-economic. (b) It does not generate income or wealth; he teaches free of charge. (c) Kavya's aunt, who conducts online classes in the evening and charges a weekly fee for them.
s: (a) Non-economic
(b) It earns no income; the classes are free
(c) Kavya's aunt, who charges a weekly fee for her online classes

questions.q:
Cooking a meal can be either kind of activity.
(a) Describe a situation in which cooking a meal is a non-economic activity.
(b) Describe a situation in which cooking a meal is an economic activity.
(c) State the one thing that changes between your two situations and decides the category.
questions.a: (a) A mother cooking food for her family at home, out of love and care, with no payment. (b) A cook in a restaurant or a caterer who cooks food for customers and is paid for it. (c) Whether the cooking is done in exchange for money or money's worth: if it is, it is economic; if it is done without income, out of love or care, it is non-economic.
s: (a) A valid unpaid situation, such as a parent cooking for the family
(b) A valid paid situation, such as a restaurant cook or caterer
(c) The deciding change: whether it is done in exchange for money or money's worth

questions.q:
Nirmala lives in Jaipur. On weekdays she works as a receptionist at a hotel, which pays her a fixed amount at the end of every month. Every evening she helps her son with his schoolwork. On Sundays she and her brothers repaint the walls of their parents' house, and nobody is paid.
(a) Classify each of her three activities as economic or non-economic.
(b) Name the chapter's term for the payment she receives from the hotel.
(c) Two of her activities take effort but earn nothing. Explain why the chapter still treats such activities as important.
(d) State the one test that decides which category any activity belongs to.
questions.a: (a) The hotel job is economic; helping her son with schoolwork and repainting her parents' house are non-economic. (b) A salary: a fixed regular payment, generally paid monthly, by an employer to an employee. (c) The chapter says non-economic activities are done out of feelings like love, care and respect, and that although they may not involve money, the value they generate is important in our lives. (d) Whether the activity involves money, or is done in exchange for money or money's worth.
s: (a) Hotel job economic; schoolwork help and repainting non-economic
(b) Salary
(c) Done out of love and care; the value they generate is important even without money
(d) The test: whether money or money's worth is involved

questions.q:
A housing society in Bhubaneswar runs a weekend reading club for 30 children. Two volunteers, Mrs. Mohanty, a retired teacher, and Aman, a college student, read stories to the children by turns; neither is paid, and the children pay nothing. The society secretary now proposes that each child pays Rs 50 a month and that each of the two readers is paid Rs 750 a month.
(a) Under the present arrangement, is the reading club an economic or a non-economic activity? Give a reason.
(b) Under the new plan, how much would the society collect in a month, and how much would be left after paying both readers?
(c) Would the readers' work under the new plan be economic or non-economic? Why?
(d) Some parents want the club to stay free. Should the society accept the new plan? Give one point in favour of each side and your decision.
questions.a: (a) Non-economic: no money changes hands; the volunteers read out of care for the children. (b) 30 x Rs 50 = Rs 1,500 collected; 2 x Rs 750 = Rs 1,500 paid out, so Rs 0 is left. (c) Economic, because the readers would be working in exchange for money. (d) For staying free: the volunteers' unpaid work is done out of care, and the chapter says the value non-economic activities generate is important even without money; it also costs families nothing. For the new plan: the readers would be paid for their time and effort, and the plan exactly covers its own cost. Either decision earns the mark if it is backed by one of these points; for example, keep it free, since the money collected would only be passed on to the readers and the club already works well on care alone.
s: (a) Non-economic, because no money changes hands and it is done out of care
(b) Rs 1,500 collected and Rs 0 left after paying Rs 1,500
(c) Economic, because the readers would work in exchange for money
(d) A decision supported by one point for each side from the chapter and the data

Match each item from Kavya's visit to Kamlapur in Column A with the form of payment in Column B.

Choose the correct option.

questions.q: What is meant by 'payment in kind'? Give the example of it from Sahil's story.
questions.a: Payment in kind is a non-cash payment received for the work performed. Sahil, a farm labourer, receives part of his daily wage in the form of mangoes of equal value; these mangoes are payment in kind.
s: Meaning: a non-cash payment received for work performed
Example: the mangoes Sahil receives as part of his wage

questions.q:
Mrs. Bhatia works as a clerk at a bank in Amritsar and is paid a fixed amount every month. On Saturdays she advises small shopkeepers on how to keep their accounts, and each shopkeeper pays her for the advice.
(a) Name the form of payment for each of her two activities.
(b) Explain why the Saturday payment is not a salary.
questions.a: (a) The bank job pays a salary; the Saturday advice earns a fee. (b) A salary is a fixed regular payment, generally monthly, by an employer to an employee. On Saturdays she has no employer: each shopkeeper pays her in exchange for professional advice, which is what the chapter calls a fee.
s: (a) Bank job: salary; Saturday advice: fee
(b) No employer paying a fixed monthly amount; each shopkeeper pays for professional advice, so it is a fee

questions.q: Jatin says: 'Sahil is paid partly in mangoes, not money, so tilling the farmer's land is a non-economic activity.' Check Jatin's claim using the chapter.
questions.a: Jatin is wrong. Economic activities are those performed in exchange for money or money's worth. Sahil earns a daily wage for his work, paid partly in cash and partly in mangoes of equal value; the mangoes are payment in kind, a non-cash payment for work performed, so they are money's worth. His work is therefore an economic activity.
s: Verdict: the claim is wrong
Economic activities include those done for money's worth, not only for money
Sahil earns a wage, part in cash and part as mangoes of equal value (payment in kind), so his work is economic

questions.q:
A new rice mill has opened in the village of Hirapur near Ranchi. Gopal runs the mill's husking machine and is paid Rs 9,000 at the end of every month by the mill owner. Lata cleans and stacks rice sacks; for each day she works she gets Rs 350, of which Rs 250 is paid in cash and the rest in rice of equal value. When the machine broke down, an engineer, Mr. Sen, came once to advise on the repair and charged Rs 2,000 for his advice.
(a) What is the chapter's term for the payment Gopal receives?
(b) What is the chapter's term for the payment Lata receives for each day of work?
(c) What is the rice Lata receives called, and what is it worth each day?
(d) What is the chapter's term for the Rs 2,000 Mr. Sen charged?
questions.a: (a) A salary: a fixed regular payment, paid monthly by an employer to an employee. (b) A (daily) wage: a payment by the employer to the worker for a specific period of time. (c) Payment in kind; it is worth Rs 350 - Rs 250 = Rs 100 a day. (d) A fee: a payment in exchange for professional advice or services.
s: (a) Salary
(b) A daily wage
(c) Payment in kind, worth Rs 100 a day
(d) A fee

questions.q:
Imran is offered two ways of being paid for picking mangoes at an orchard in Malihabad during a 30-day season.
Plan A: a daily wage of Rs 450, all in cash.
Plan B: a daily wage of Rs 400 in cash plus 2 kg of mangoes each day. Mangoes sell for Rs 60 per kg in the local market.
(a) What is the chapter's term for the mangoes in Plan B?
(b) What is Plan B worth for one day?
(c) What is each plan worth if he works all 30 days?
(d) Imran's family can sell the mangoes in the local market at that price. Which plan should he choose, and by how much is it better over the season?
(e) His neighbour says, 'Under Plan B, part of Imran's work stops being an economic activity, because it is not paid in money.' Correct the neighbour.
questions.a: (a) Payment in kind. (b) Rs 400 + 2 x Rs 60 = Rs 520 a day. (c) Plan A: 30 x Rs 450 = Rs 13,500; Plan B: 30 x Rs 520 = Rs 15,600. (d) Plan B, which is worth Rs 15,600 - Rs 13,500 = Rs 2,100 more over the season (if the mangoes can be sold at Rs 60 per kg). (e) Economic activities are those done in exchange for money or money's worth. The mangoes are a non-cash payment for work performed, so all of Imran's picking work is still an economic activity, just as Sahil's is in the chapter.
s: (a) Payment in kind
(b) Rs 520 a day
(c) Plan A Rs 13,500 and Plan B Rs 15,600
(d) Chooses Plan B, Rs 2,100 better
(e) Payment in kind is money's worth, so the work stays economic

questions.q: Rajesh buys wood for Rs 600 and sells a chair made from it for Rs 1,000. What does the chapter say the remaining Rs 400 stands for?
questions.a: The monetary value of Rajesh's skill, time and effort
o: The monetary value of Rajesh's skill, time and effort
The price Rajesh paid for the wood at the market
A fee Rajesh pays to the market for selling there

questions.q: A weaver in Varanasi buys silk thread for Rs 1,800 and sells the sari she weaves from it for Rs 4,500. Using the chapter's method, what value has she added?
Cotton grown by a farmer is spun into yarn, the yarn is woven into cloth, and the cloth is stitched into a kurta. According to the chapter, where does value addition happen in this chain?
questions.a: At each stage where the material is turned into another form
o: At each stage where the material is turned into another form
Only at the last stage, when the finished kurta is sold
Only at the first stage, when the cotton is grown
Nowhere, because the same cotton is used all along

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Rajesh adds value to the wood by turning it into furniture.
Reason (R): The Rs 400 left after paying for the wood is the amount Rajesh spends on his special tools.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: True or False? 'In the chapter's example, Rajesh's buying of wood and his selling of the chair are both economic activities.' Give the verdict and a reason.
questions.a: True. The chapter says that from buying the wood to selling the chair, these activities involve payment, so they are a part of economic activities.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: both buying the wood and selling the chair involve payment

questions.q:
A carpenter in Saharanpur buys wood for Rs 2,350 and sells a cupboard made from it for Rs 5,000.
(a) Find the value he has added.
(b) According to the chapter, what does this amount stand for?
questions.a: (a) Rs 5,000 - Rs 2,350 = Rs 2,650. (b) The monetary value of the carpenter's skill, time and effort that went into making the cupboard.
s: (a) Value added = Rs 2,650
(b) The monetary value of his skill, time and effort

questions.q:
Shalini, who runs a small jam unit in Shimla, buys 10 kg of apples for Rs 900. She turns them into jam and sells all the jars for Rs 2,400.
(a) What is value addition, according to the chapter?
(b) What value has Shalini added?
(c) At which step of her work is this value added?
questions.a: (a) Value addition is the value that economic activities add at each stage of the process of transforming something into another form. (b) Rs 2,400 - Rs 900 = Rs 1,500. (c) When she transforms the apples into jam, a new form that sells for more than the apples cost.
s: (a) Value added at each stage of transforming something into another form
(c) When the apples are transformed into jam

questions.q: Rajesh's friend says: 'If Rajesh had sold the chair for only Rs 600, he would have added no value, so making and selling that chair would not be an economic activity at all.' Is the friend right, wrong, or partly right? Explain.
questions.a: Partly right. The first part is correct: the value added would be Rs 600 - Rs 600 = Rs 0, so no money would be left to pay for his skill, time and effort. The second part is wrong: buying the wood and selling the chair would still involve payment, and the chapter says activities that involve payment are economic activities.
s: Verdict: partly right
Correct part: value added would be Rs 0
Wrong part: buying wood and selling the chair still involve payment, so they remain economic

questions.q:
In Tiruppur, a cotton farmer sells raw cotton to a spinning mill for Rs 3,000. The mill spins it into yarn and sells the yarn to a weaver for Rs 5,200. The weaver weaves the yarn into cloth and sells it to a garment unit for Rs 8,000. The garment unit stitches the cloth into shirts and sells all of them for Rs 14,500.
(a) What value did the spinning mill add?
(b) What value did the weaver add?
(c) Which of the three stages after the farmer added the most value, and how much?
(d) Show that the values added by the mill, the weaver and the garment unit together equal the final price of the shirts minus the price of the raw cotton, and explain what this shows about the chapter's idea of value addition.
questions.a: (a) Rs 5,200 - Rs 3,000 = Rs 2,200. (b) Rs 8,000 - Rs 5,200 = Rs 2,800. (c) The garment unit: Rs 14,500 - Rs 8,000 = Rs 6,500. (d) Rs 2,200 + Rs 2,800 + Rs 6,500 = Rs 11,500, and Rs 14,500 - Rs 3,000 = Rs 11,500. This shows that value is added at each stage of transforming something into another form, and the final price is built up stage by stage.
s: (c) The garment unit, Rs 6,500
(d) Both totals are Rs 11,500; value is added at each stage of transforming the material

questions.q:
A women's self-help group in Kutch makes embroidered cloth bags. For one batch of 20 bags, they buy cloth for Rs 1,600 and coloured thread for Rs 400. They sell every bag for Rs 250.
(a) What is the total cost of the raw materials for the batch?
(b) How much do they get by selling the whole batch?
(c) What value does the group add to the batch?
(d) What value is added to each bag?
(e) According to the chapter, what does this added value stand for?
questions.a: (a) Rs 1,600 + Rs 400 = Rs 2,000. (b) 20 x Rs 250 = Rs 5,000. (c) Rs 5,000 - Rs 2,000 = Rs 3,000. (d) Rs 3,000 / 20 = Rs 150 per bag. (e) The monetary value of the group's skill, time and effort that went into turning the cloth and thread into bags.
s: (a) Raw materials cost Rs 2,000
(b) Sales of Rs 5,000
(c) Value added Rs 3,000
(d) Rs 150 per bag
(e) The monetary value of their skill, time and effort

questions.q:

Choose the correct option.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: True or False? 'The free food served to visitors at a langar is an example of payment in kind.' Give the verdict and a reason.
questions.a: False. Payment in kind is a non-cash payment received for work performed, like Sahil's mangoes. The langar serves food to every visitor for free, not as payment for any work; it is an example of seva, or selfless service.

questions.q: State two ways in which practices of seva are valuable, according to the chapter.
questions.a: (1) They foster a sense of satisfaction and gratitude for what we have. (2) They are a way of contributing to society without expecting anything in return.
s: Foster a sense of satisfaction and gratitude for what we have
A way of contributing to society without expecting anything in return

questions.q:
During floods in Assam, members of a church in Guwahati cook meals and hand them out free to families who have lost their homes. They ask for nothing in return.
(a) What is the chapter's word for this kind of service?
(b) Is it an economic or a non-economic activity?
(c) State one way in which such practices are valuable, according to the chapter.
questions.a: (a) Seva (selfless service). (b) Non-economic, because it involves no money and nothing is expected in return. (c) Such practices foster a sense of satisfaction and gratitude for what we have (or: they are a way of contributing to society without expecting anything in return).

(b) Non-economic: no money, nothing expected in return
(c) Fosters satisfaction and gratitude, or contributes to society without expecting anything in return

questions.q: A langar at a gurudwara and a roadside dhaba next to it both serve dal and roti to hundreds of people every day. Using the chapter's ideas, explain three differences between them.
questions.a: (1) Money: the dhaba sells its meals to customers for money, while the langar serves food to every visitor for free. (2) Category: the dhaba's cooking and selling is an economic activity; the langar is a non-economic activity, an example of seva. (3) Purpose: the dhaba works to earn income, while the langar is a way of contributing to society without expecting anything in return, and it fosters satisfaction and gratitude.
s: Money: the dhaba sells meals; the langar serves every visitor free
Category: the dhaba is economic; the langar is non-economic (seva)
Purpose: income for the dhaba; contributing to society without expecting anything in return for the langar

questions.q:
Harleen's class in Amritsar is making a poster titled 'Seva'. The poster has four empty lines. Write what should go on each line, using the chapter.
(a) What seva means.
(b) The name for the community kitchens at gurudwaras that serve every visitor for free.
(c) The two feelings that practices of seva foster.
(d) What a person doing seva expects in return.
questions.a: (a) Selfless service. (b) Langars. (c) Satisfaction and gratitude (for what we have). (d) Nothing; seva contributes to society without expecting anything in return.
s: (a) Selfless service
(b) Langars
(c) Satisfaction and gratitude
(d) Nothing in return

questions.q:
At a busy religious fair in Ujjain, Neel notices five activities. For each, write 'seva' or 'economic activity', with a reason in a few words.
(a) Volunteers sweeping the fair ground every evening without any payment.
(b) A flower seller selling garlands to visitors.
(c) Volunteers serving free meals to every visitor at a community kitchen.
(d) A photographer charging visitors for printed photographs.
(e) A group of young people giving free drinking water to tired pilgrims.
questions.a: (a) Seva: unpaid service, nothing expected in return. (b) Economic activity: garlands are sold for money. (c) Seva: free meals to every visitor, like a langar. (d) Economic activity: the photographer is paid for the photographs. (e) Seva: free help to pilgrims without expecting anything in return.
s: (a) Seva: unpaid, nothing expected in return
(b) Economic: garlands sold for money
(c) Seva: free meals to every visitor
(d) Economic: paid for photographs
(e) Seva: free water, nothing expected in return

questions.q: The chapter describes Van Mahotsav as the festival of:
questions.a: Forests

Harvests

questions.q: According to the chapter, what do the individual and the collective efforts of citizens under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan together lead to?
questions.a: A clean home, neighbourhood, society and nation

questions.q:
Read these statements from the chapter's section on community participation.
I. Van Mahotsav is celebrated to promote awareness about the value of trees and the conservation of forests.
II. Under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, people have come together to clean streets, roads, parks and other public places.
III. The chapter gives the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and Van Mahotsav as examples of collective community participation.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I, II and III
o: I, II and III
I and II only
II and III only
I and III only

questions.q:
Match each example from the chapter in Column A with the idea it illustrates in Column B.
Column A: 1. A langar at a gurudwara  2. Van Mahotsav  3. The mangoes given to Sahil  4. The Rs 400 left from Rajesh's chair
Column B: P. payment in kind  Q. seva  R. collective community participation  S. value addition
What is the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan based on, according to the chapter? Name two kinds of public places that people have come together to clean.
questions.a: It is based on the collective efforts of all Indian citizens to keep our surroundings clean. People have come together to clean up streets, roads, parks and other public places or community areas (any two).
s: Based on the collective efforts of all citizens to keep surroundings clean
Any two of: streets, roads, parks, other public places or community areas

questions.q:
In Kanpur, a municipal sweeper is paid a fixed amount every month to sweep Station Road. On a Sunday, a group of residents also cleans the same road together as part of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.
(a) Is the sweeper's work economic or non-economic? Why?
(b) Is the residents' Sunday cleaning economic or non-economic? Why?
questions.a: (a) Economic, because the sweeper is paid a salary, a fixed regular monthly payment, for the work. (b) Non-economic, because the residents earn nothing for it; it is collective community participation done to keep their surroundings clean.
s: (a) Economic: the sweeper is paid a salary for the work
(b) Non-economic: unpaid collective community participation to keep surroundings clean

questions.q: Tanvi says: 'Van Mahotsav tree-plantation drives and Swachh Bharat clean-ups take a lot of people's time and effort, but they are still non-economic activities.' Is Tanvi right? Explain using the chapter.
questions.a: Yes, Tanvi is right. What makes an activity economic is that it involves money or is done in exchange for money or money's worth, not how much time or effort it takes. In both, members of the community come together without payment, as collective community participation, to plant trees or keep their surroundings clean. The chapter says that although non-economic activities may not involve money, the value they generate is important in our lives.
s: Verdict: Tanvi is right
Payment, not time or effort, decides whether an activity is economic
Both are unpaid collective community participation whose value is still important

questions.q:
A school in Dehradun can hold only one community event in July. There are two proposals.
Proposal 1: a clean-up of the street and park around the school. A survey after a recent fair found 40 bags of litter left in the park.
Proposal 2: a tree-plantation drive on the hillside behind the school. The forest department has offered 300 saplings, but only for this July.
(a) Which national initiative described in the chapter does Proposal 1 follow, and what is its aim?
(b) Which celebration described in the chapter does Proposal 2 follow, and what does it promote?
(c) Explain why both proposals are non-economic activities of the same kind.
(d) Choose one proposal for July and justify your choice using the data.
questions.a: (a) The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, which is based on the collective efforts of all citizens to keep our surroundings clean. (b) Van Mahotsav, the festival of forests, which promotes awareness about the value of trees and the conservation of forests through tree-plantation drives. (c) Both involve no payment and bring members of the community together for a shared goal; the chapter calls this collective community participation. (d) Either choice is acceptable with a data-based reason. For example, Proposal 2, because the 300 saplings are available only this July, while a clean-up can be held in another month; or Proposal 1, because the 40 bags of litter are a problem in the park right now.
s: (a) Swachh Bharat Abhiyan: collective efforts to keep surroundings clean
(b) Van Mahotsav: awareness of the value of trees and conservation of forests
(c) Both unpaid and bring the community together: collective community participation
(d) A clear choice justified with the data (saplings only this July, or 40 bags of litter now)

questions.q:
For Van Mahotsav, a residents' association in Nagpur plans to plant saplings along a 1.2 km road. A government nursery gives the association 240 saplings free of charge. Forty-eight residents volunteer, and each of them will plant the same number of saplings. A contractor has also offered to do all the planting for Rs 6,000.
(a) What does Van Mahotsav aim to promote, according to the chapter?
(b) If the 48 volunteers do the planting, how many saplings will each plant?
(c) If the contractor does it, how much is paid for each sapling planted?
(d) Which option is a non-economic, collective community activity and which is an economic activity? Recommend one option for the association's Van Mahotsav, with a reason.
questions.a: (a) Awareness about the value of trees and the conservation of forests. (b) 240 / 48 = 5 saplings each. (c) Rs 6,000 / 240 = Rs 25 per sapling. (d) The volunteers' planting is a non-economic, collective community activity; the contractor's planting is economic because it is done for payment. Recommended: the volunteer option, because Van Mahotsav brings members of the community together for tree-plantation drives to spread awareness, and it costs nothing; the contractor option would save the residents' time but costs Rs 6,000 and leaves the residents out.
s: (a) Awareness of the value of trees and the conservation of forests
(b) 5 saplings each
(c) Rs 25 per sapling
(d) Volunteers non-economic, contractor economic, with a reasoned recommendation

questions.a: (a) Some activities earn no income, yet they still create value for people and society. (b) Seva, selfless service seen in temples, gurudwaras, mosques and churches (such as langars serving every visitor free), fosters satisfaction and gratitude and contributes to society without expecting anything in return. (c) Under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, citizens keep homes and public places clean; together these efforts lead to a clean home, neighbourhood, society and nation. (d) Van Mahotsav brings the community together for tree-plantation drives and promotes awareness about the value of trees and the conservation of forests. (e) Social welfare, personal wellbeing and the overall quality of life.
s: (a) Meaning: no income, but real value for people and society
(b) Seva: fosters satisfaction and gratitude, contributes without expecting a return
(c) Swachh Bharat Abhiyan: clean home, neighbourhood, society and nation
(d) Van Mahotsav: awareness of the value of trees and forest conservation
(e) Social welfare, personal wellbeing and quality of life
